name: Question 6
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191664/assets/2334f6ee136334c70b658c41a6bc0ec578b135c7c6bc9ef87a0f8d156a7db01c.png)

What is the union of the intervals shown on the number lines above?
worked_solution:
We have the following number lines:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191664/assets/2334f6ee136334c70b658c41a6bc0ec578b135c7c6bc9ef87a0f8d156a7db01c.png)

The union of the two intervals consists of all the points which are contained within at least one of the intervals. So, to graph the union of the two intervals, we take the graphs of the individual intervals and lay them on top of each other.

The resulting graph is as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191664/assets/32899816340ae23edc2fdca86e13a1d04e04af1e5723beda1a684c6e51e16f4d.png)

The corresponding inequality is $x\le 1.$
